title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON PHARMACOLOGIC TREATMENT OF SEX OFFENDERS' SEXUAL IMPULSES
title_original: 성폭력범죄자의 성충동 약물치료에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters mandated by the Act on Pharmacologic Treatment of Sex Offenders' Sexual Impulses and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

CHAPTER II REQUESTS FOR MEDICAL TREATMENT ORDERS

Article 2 (Diagnosis and evaluation by psychiatrists) (1) Pursuant to Article 4(2) and (6) of the Act on Pharmacologic Treatment of Sex Offenders' Sexual Impulses (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"), before requesting an order for pharmacologic treatment of sexual impulses under Article 4(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "medical treatment order"), a prosecutor shall request a psychiatrist of any of the following facilities or institutions to conduct a diagnosis or evaluation regarding a person subject to a request for a medical treatment order (hereinafter referred to as the "respondent to a medical treatment order request"): <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011; Nov. 29, 2016; May 29, 2017>
  1. A medical treatment and custody facility under the Act on Medical Treatment and Custody (hereinafter referred to as a "medical treatment and custody facility");
  2. An institution designated by the Minister of Justice from among psychiatric medical institutions under the Act on the Improvement of Mental Health and the Support for Welfare Services for Mental Patients.
  (2) A psychiatrist who conducts a diagnosis or evaluation under paragraph (1) shall personally interview the respondent to a medical treatment order request and shall conduct the diagnosis or evaluation, and may use psychological or physiological evaluation tools if necessary for the diagnosis or evaluation. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011>
  [Title Amended on Nov. 23, 2011]

Article 3 (Investigation) (1) When requesting an investigation from the head of a probation office (including a branch office; hereinafter the same shall apply) under Article 5(1) of the Act, a prosecutor shall notify the head of the probation office of the personal information of the respondent to a medical treatment order request and a summary of the criminal facts. In such cases, the prosecutor may also send reference data prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Justice.
  (2) If necessary for an investigation under Article 5(1) of the Act, the head of a probation office may request necessary cooperation from the head of a correctional institution, juvenile correctional institution, detention center, or military correctional institution (hereinafter referred to as a "confinement facility"), the chief of a police station, or the head of a medical treatment and custody facility. In such cases, the head of the requested institution shall comply with the request unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.

Article 4 (Matters to be stated in request for a medical treatment order) (1) "Matters by which the respondent to a medical treatment order request can be identified" in Article 7(1)1 of the Act means the following:
  1. The resident registration number of the respondent to a medical treatment order request;
  2. Place of residence;
  3. Occupation;
  4. Registered domicile.
  (2) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 7(1)4 of the Act means the following:
  1. The name of the offense committed by the respondent to a medical treatment order request;
  2. Contact information;
  3. Whether the respondent is under detention;
  4. The name of the defense counsel.

Article 4-2 (Application for exemption from execution of a medical treatment order) (1) A person who intends to apply for exemption from execution of a medical treatment order under Article 8-2(1) through (3) of the Act shall submit an application form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Justice to the district court (including a branch court) having jurisdiction over the person's place of residence or current location.
  (2) If a court requests the head of a probation office to investigate necessary matters under Article 8-2(5) of the Act, it shall notify the head of the probation office of the personal information of the person issued with a medical treatment order and a summary of the criminal facts. In such cases, the court may transmit reference data if it deems it necessary.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 29, 2017]

Article 5 (Psychological treatment programs, including cognitive behavioral therapy) (1) The psychological treatment programs, including cognitive behavioral therapy, under Article 10(1)3 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "psychological treatment programs") shall include the following:
  1. Correction of cognitive distortions and deviant sexual preferences;
  2. Enhancement of motivation for treatment;
  3. Promotion of empathy for victims;
  4. Development of social adjustment skills;
  5. Prevention of the recurrence of deviant sexual behavior;
  6. Other matters necessary for preventing recidivism of sexual offenses.
  (2) Psychological treatment programs shall be conducted at least once a month during the period of pharmacologic treatment of sexual impulses (hereinafter referred to as "pharmacologic treatment").
  (3) The Minister of Justice shall endeavor to develop psychological treatment programs and foster professional personnel for their implementation.

CHAPTER III EXECUTION OF MEDICAL TREATMENT ORDERS

Article 6 (Directions for execution) (1) Where a judgment imposing a medical treatment order becomes final and conclusive, the prosecutor shall, without delay, send a written direction under Article 13(2) of the Act to the head of the probation office having jurisdiction over the place of residence of the person sentenced to the medical treatment order (hereinafter referred to as the "person issued with a medical treatment order").
  (2) The written direction under paragraph (1) shall be accompanied by the evaluation report prepared by a psychiatrist under Article 4(2) of the Act. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011>

Article 7 (Execution of medical treatment orders) (1) Before executing a medical treatment order under Article 13(1) of the Act, a probation officer shall verify all of the following documents: <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011; Dec. 29, 2017>
  1. A certified copy of the judgment concerning the person issued with a medical treatment order;
  2. The written direction under Article 6(1);
  3. The evaluation report prepared by a psychiatrist under Article 6(2);
  4. A certified copy of the written decision on exemption from execution of a medical treatment order transmitted under Article 8-4 of the Act.
  (2) Before executing a medical treatment order, a probation officer shall inform the person issued with a medical treatment order of all of the following matters:
  1. The matters to be observed under Article 10 of the Act;
  2. The obligations of a person issued with a medical treatment order under Article 15 of the Act and this Decree;
  3. Matters concerning the extension of the treatment period under Article 16 of the Act;
  4. Matters concerning the penalties under Article 35 of the Act.
  (3) When executing a medical treatment order by administering medication, a probation officer shall administer the medication in accordance with the diagnosis and prescription of a physician of a treatment institution and shall conduct hormone level tests together with the administration of the medication.

Article 8 (Designation of medication for treatment) (1) The medications to be administered to a person issued with a medical treatment order under Article 14(1) of the Act shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Justice from among any of the following medications:
  1. Medication that suppresses or reduces the production of sex hormones;
  2. Medications that inhibit the binding of sex hormones to their receptors.
  (2) When designating and publicly notifying medications under paragraph (1), the Minister of Justice shall hear the opinions of relevant experts, including psychiatrists and urologists. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011; Nov. 21, 2017>

Article 9 (Treatment institutions) (1) Under Article 14(1) and (6) of the Act, a probation officer may have any of the following facilities or institutions (each of which is hereinafter referred to as a "treatment institution") administer pharmacologic treatment: <Amended on May 29, 2017>
  1. The facilities or institutions specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2(1);
  2. Institutions designated by the Minister of Justice from among psychiatric medical institutions under the Act on the Improvement of Mental Health and the Support for Welfare Services for Mental Patients, other than those referred to in subparagraph 1.
  (2) The full amount of treatment expenses shall be paid, within the budget, to a treatment institution that has administered pharmacologic treatment under paragraph (1).

Article 10 (Transfer of inmates confined in confinement facilities) (1) The head of a confinement facility in which a person issued with a medical treatment order is confined shall transfer such person to a medical treatment and custody facility under Article 37(2) of the Act on Execution of Sentences and Treatment of Inmates not earlier than 3 months and not later than 2 months before the person's release due to completion of, or exemption from, the execution of a sentence, parole, or any similar reason.
  (2) Where a person issued with a medical treatment order is transferred under paragraph (1), the head of the medical treatment and custody facility shall notify the head of the probation office having jurisdiction over the person's place of residence thereof without delay.
  (3) The head of a medical treatment and custody facility shall notify the head of the probation office having jurisdiction over the place of residence of a person issued with a medical treatment order of the scheduled release of such person no later than 5 days before the person's release due to completion of, or exemption from, the execution of a sentence or medical treatment and custody, parole, provisional termination of medical treatment and custody, or any similar reason.

Article 11 (Examination and treatment of adverse effects) (1) Where a medical treatment order is executed by administering medication, a probation officer shall have a physician of a treatment institution conduct examinations and provide treatment for adverse effects in conjunction with the administration of the medication. In such cases, where it is difficult for the treatment institution to conduct examinations and provide treatment for adverse effects, the probation officer may have the head of the treatment institution arrange for such examinations and treatment in cooperation with a medical institution under the Medical Service Act (hereinafter referred to as a "medical institution").
  (2) Where, as a result of an examination under paragraph (1), a physician is of the opinion that irreparable harm may occur to the body of a person issued with a medical treatment order, or where adverse effects resulting from the administration of medication are otherwise deemed significant, the probation officer may temporarily suspend the administration of the medication.
  (3) Where the administration of medication is temporarily suspended under paragraph (2), the head of the probation office to which the probation officer belongs shall immediately apply in writing to the Probation Review Commission under Article 5 of the Act on Probation (hereinafter referred to as the "Review Commission") for approval of the temporary suspension of the administration of medication.
  (4) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (3), the Review Commission shall decide without delay whether to approve the temporary suspension of the administration of medication. In such cases, the Review Commission may request a medical institution to diagnose adverse effects arising from pharmacologic treatment administered to the person issued with a medical treatment order.
  (5) From the date on which approval of the temporary suspension of the administration of medication is granted under paragraph (4), the probation officer shall, every month, report to the Review Commission on the results of a physician's diagnosis and prescription concerning the treatment of adverse effects, changes in physical condition, and the suitability of continued administration of medication for the person issued with a medical treatment order.
  (6) Based on the report submitted by the probation officer under paragraph (5), the Review Commission shall examine and decide whether to resume the administration of medication.
  (7) Where the Review Commission dismisses an application under paragraph (3) or decides under paragraph (6) that the administration of medication should be resumed, the probation officer shall, without delay, resume execution of the medical treatment order.

Article 12 (Execution of remaining period of a medical treatment order whose execution has been suspended) (1) Under Article 14(4) of the Act, the remaining period of a medical treatment order whose execution has been suspended shall be executed as follows:
  1. Where execution has been suspended due to any of the grounds specified in Article 14(4)2 or 3 of the Act and the period during which the person is to serve the sentence, medical treatment and custody, or protective custody is at least 3 months: The medical treatment order shall be executed under Article 14(3) of the Act and Article 10 of this Decree;
  2. In cases other than those specified in subparagraph 1: A probation officer having jurisdiction over the place of residence of the person issued with a medical treatment order shall execute the medical treatment order for the remaining period.
  (2) In cases under paragraph (1)2, the person issued with a medical treatment order shall appear and report to the probation office having jurisdiction over his or her place of residence within 10 days from the date of release and shall comply with the probation officer's directions regarding the execution of the medical treatment order.
  (3) The execution period of a medical treatment order under paragraph (1) shall recommence on the date on which administration of the treatment medication is resumed.
  (4) Where grounds arise for execution of the remaining period of a medical treatment order under Article 14(5) of the Act, the head of a confinement facility or medical treatment and custody facility shall notify the head of the probation office having jurisdiction over the place of residence of the person whose medical treatment order has been suspended of the scheduled release of such person no later than 5 days before the person's release.

Article 13 (Obligations of persons issued with medical treatment orders) (1) Where it is necessary to verify whether a person issued with a medical treatment order complies with the obligations under Article 15(1) of the Act, a probation officer may conduct hormone level tests or tests to determine whether counteracting medications have been administered.
  (2) Where a probation officer directs the submission of urine or other specimens for the tests under paragraph (1), the person issued with a medical treatment order shall comply therewith.
  (3) The head of a probation office shall send urine or other specimens submitted by a person issued with a medical treatment order to the Supreme Prosecutors' Office or the National Forensic Service and request the tests under paragraph (1). <Amended on Dec. 30, 2015>

Article 14 (Permission for change of residence, domestic travel, and departure from the Republic of Korea) (1) Upon receipt of an application for permission for a change of residence or any similar matter under Article 15(3) of the Act, a probation officer shall decide whether to grant permission within 7 days from the date of receipt of the application, taking into comprehensive consideration the following matters:
  1. The intended new residence, destination of domestic travel, or destination outside the Republic of Korea;
  2. The reason for the change of residence, the purpose of domestic travel, or the purpose of departure from the Republic of Korea;
  3. The expected period of stay outside the Republic of Korea;
  4. The progress of treatment and the status of compliance with the matters to be observed;
  5. Whether there is a purpose to evade the medical treatment order.
  (2) Where a person issued with a medical treatment order obtains permission for a change of residence under Article 15(3) of the Act and changes his or her residence to the jurisdiction of another probation office, he or she shall, within 3 days, appear at and report the change of residence to the probation office having jurisdiction over the new place of residence.
  (3) Where a probation officer of a probation office permits a person issued with a medical treatment order to depart from the Republic of Korea under paragraph (1), the head of the probation office may request the head of an agency responsible for immigration affairs to notify the probation office of the person's entry into and departure from the Republic of Korea.

Article 15 (Application for extension of the treatment period) (1) When the head of a probation office applies for an extension of the treatment period or an addition to or modification of the matters to be observed under Article 16(1) or (2) of the Act, he or she shall do so in writing stating the following matters:
  1. The name, resident registration number, place of residence, and occupation of the person issued with a medical treatment order;
  2. Purport of a request;
  3. Grounds necessitating the extension of the treatment period or the addition or modification of matters to be observed.
  (2) When filing an application under paragraph (1), the head of the probation office shall submit data substantiating the grounds for the application.
  (3) If necessary for the hearing of a request under Article 16 of the Act, the court may require the responsible probation officer to appear and provide his or her opinion, and may summon and examine the person issued with a medical treatment order or verify any necessary matters.

Article 16 (Application for provisional rescission from medical treatment order) (1) An application for provisional rescission from a medical treatment order under Article 17(1) of the Act shall be filed with the Review Commission in writing.
  (2) Where a person issued with a medical treatment order or his or her legal representative applies for provisional rescission from the medical treatment order, the Review Commission shall notify the head of the probation office thereof without delay.

Article 17 (Examination and decision on provisional rescission of medical treatment order) (1) When the Review Commission examines a provisional rescission of a medical treatment order under Article 18(1) of the Act, it shall hear the opinions of the psychiatrist who administered the treatment and the probation officer, and may, if necessary, hear the opinions of other experts. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011>
  (2) When the Review Commission makes a decision under Article 18(4) and (5) of the Act, it shall, without delay, serve a certified copy of the written decision on the head of the competent probation office and the applicant.
  (3) Allowances or expenses may be paid, within the budget, to a psychiatrist, other experts, etc. who have submitted opinions or data to the Review Commission under paragraph (1). <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011>

Article 18 (Revocation of provisional rescission) (1) An application for the revocation of provisional rescission under Article 19(1) of the Act shall be submitted to the Review Commission in writing.
  (2) When the Review Commission makes a decision to revoke the provisional rescission of a medical treatment order under Article 19(1) of the Act, it shall, without delay, notify the head of the competent probation office and the person whose provisional rescission is revoked of such fact.
  (3) Where provisional rescission is revoked, the execution period of the medical treatment order shall run from the date on which sex hormone regulating medicine is administered for the first time after the revocation of the provisional rescission.

CHAPTER IV MEDICAL TREATMENT ORDERS FOR INMATES AND PERSONS WHOSE EXECUTION IS PROVISIONALLY TERMINATED

Article 19 (Explanations by head of confinement facility and verification of consent) The head of a confinement facility shall present and explain matters regarding pharmacologic treatment in writing under Article 22(2)1 of the Act to an inmate who has committed a sexual assault crime under Article 22(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an “inmate convicted of sexual assault”) and who has been selected as a person subject to an application for parole eligibility review under Article 121(1) of the Act on Execution of Sentences and Treatment of Inmates, and where the inmate consents to the pharmacologic treatment, such consent shall be verified in writing.

Article 20 (Notification by head of confinement facility) Where an inmate convicted of sexual assault consents to pharmacologic treatment under Article 19, the head of the confinement facility shall, without delay, notify a prosecutor of the District Prosecutors’ Office (including a branch office) having jurisdiction over the location of the confinement facility of the following matters:
  1. Inmate record files;
  2. A copy of the written judgment;
  3. A classified treatment and assessment form.

Article 21 (Investigation) When requesting an investigation from the head of a probation office under Article 22(2)3 of the Act, a prosecutor shall provide notification of the matters specified in the subparagraphs of Article 20

Article 22 (Prosecutor's request for medical treatment order) (1) When a prosecutor verifies whether an inmate convicted of sexual assault consents to pharmacologic treatment under Article 22(2)5 of the Act, the prosecutor shall provide, in writing, explanations regarding pharmacologic treatment and, where the inmate convicted of sexual assault consents thereto, shall confirm such consent in writing.
  (2) With respect to the diagnosis or evaluation by a psychiatrist and the request for a medical treatment order under Article 22(2)5 of the Act, Articles 2 and 4 of this Decree shall apply mutatis mutandis, respectively. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011>

Article 23 (Notification of request for medical treatment order) Where a prosecutor requests a medical treatment order against an inmate convicted of sexual assault under Article 22(2)5 of the Act, the prosecutor shall, without delay, send a copy of the written request to the respondent to the medical treatment order request.

Article 24 (Directions for execution) (1) Where a decision on a medical treatment order has been made under Article 22(2)6 of the Act, a prosecutor shall, without delay, notify the head of the confinement facility accommodating the inmate convicted of sexual assault of such fact.
  (2) Where a decision on a medical treatment order has been made under Article 22(2)6 of the Act, Article 6 of this Decree shall apply mutatis mutandis to the prosecutor's direction for execution.

Article 25 (Transmission of written decision on medical treatment order) Within 3 days from the date on which a medical treatment order is notified to an inmate convicted of sexual assault under Article 22(2)6 of the Act, the court shall transmit a certified copy of the written decision to the head of the probation office having jurisdiction over the place of residence of the person who has been notified of the medical treatment order.

Article 26 (Bearing of expenses) (1) A probation officer shall, in writing, order a person subject to a decision on a medical treatment order under Article 22(2)6 of the Act to pay medical treatment expenses, specifying the exact amount for each treatment procedure.
  (2) A person who has been issued a medical treatment order shall pay the medical treatment expenses within 30 days from the date of receipt of the written order referred to in paragraph (1).
  (3) Where a person who has been issued a medical treatment order lacks the financial ability to bear the medical treatment expenses, the person shall, upon each receipt of a written order to pay such expenses under paragraph (1), submit the following documents to a probation officer and obtain a decision that the State shall bear such expenses:
  1. An application for State bearing of medical treatment expenses;
  2. Where no income tax return is filed due to the absence of income, data verifying such fact;
  3. Other data verifying the absence of a regular source of income or property.
  (4) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (3), a probation officer shall verify the following administrative information through administrative data matching under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act; provided, where the applicant does not consent to such verification, the applicant shall submit the relevant documents:
  1. A certificate of amount of income (only in cases of having income);
  2. A certificate of local tax assessment and payment by tax item;
  3. A certificate of receipt of National Basic Livelihood Security benefits.
  (5) Where necessary for making a decision under paragraph (3), a probation officer may request a person who has been issued a medical treatment order to appear or submit data, or may, with the consent of such person, request public institutions, private organizations, etc., to submit data necessary for verifying the ability of the person to bear medical treatment expenses.
  (6) When requesting public institutions, private organizations, etc., to submit data necessary for verifying the ability to bear medical treatment expenses under paragraph (5), a probation officer shall attach a written consent from the person who has been issued the medical treatment order, stating the following matters:
  1. The institution that will receive the submitted data;
  2. The institution or organization that will submit the data;
  3. The scope of the data to be submitted;
  4. The validity period of the written consent;
  5. The date of preparation of the written consent;
  6. The name of the applicant, and the applicant's signature, seal, or thumbprint.
  (7) Where a probation officer decides under paragraph (3) that the medical treatment expenses shall be borne by the State, the probation officer shall pay the full amount of the expenses to the treatment institution for each treatment procedure, within the budget.

Article 27 (Request for evaluation by Medical Treatment and Custody Deliberation Committee) (1) If the Medical Treatment and Custody Deliberation Committee under Article 37 of the Act on Medical Treatment and Custody (hereinafter referred to as the "Medical Treatment and Custody Deliberation Committee") deems it necessary to impose a medical treatment order on a person whose execution is provisionally terminated, etc. under Article 25(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "person whose execution is provisionally terminated, etc."), the Medical Treatment and Custody Deliberation Committee shall request a psychiatrist at a medical treatment and custody facility to conduct a diagnosis and evaluation. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011; Nov. 29, 2016>
  (2) When it is difficult to determine whether a person has a paraphilic disorder solely on the basis of the diagnosis and evaluation conducted by a psychiatrist of a medical treatment and custody facility under paragraph (1), the Medical Treatment and Custody Deliberation Committee may request another psychiatrist to conduct an additional diagnosis and evaluation. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2011>
  (3) Where the Medical Treatment and Custody Deliberation Committee requests a diagnosis and evaluation of a person under protective custody under paragraph (1), the head of the protective custody facility shall transfer such person to a medical treatment and custody facility under Article 37(2) of the Act on Execution of Sentences and Treatment of Inmates.

Article 28 (Notification of decision on medical treatment order for persons whose execution is provisionally terminated, etc.) (1) Where the Medical Treatment and Custody Deliberation Committee imposes a medical treatment order under Article 25(1) of the Act, it shall serve the written decision on the person whose execution is provisionally terminated, etc. and a certified copy of the written decision on the head of the medical treatment and custody facility or protective custody facility (hereinafter referred to as a "custody facility"), respectively.
  (2) Upon receipt of a certified copy of the written decision under paragraph (1), the head of the custody facility shall inform the person under medical treatment and custody or the person under protective custody who is to be subject to the medical treatment order of the details, methods, procedures, effects, and adverse effects of pharmacologic treatment.

Article 29 (Application mutatis mutandis) (1) Articles 7 through 14 and Articles 16 through 18 of this Decree shall apply mutatis mutandis to medical treatment orders under Chapter IV (Articles 22 through 29) of the Act.
  (2) In addition to the provisions applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to paragraph (1), Articles 4, 6, and 15 of this Decree shall apply mutatis mutandis to medical treatment orders under Article 22 of the Act.

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 30 (Processing of sensitive information and personally identifiable information) (1) Where unavoidable for performing any of the following business affairs, a prosecutor may process information concerning health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act, information constituting criminal history records under subparagraph 2 of Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act, and data containing a resident registration number or foreigner registration number under subparagraph 1 or 4 of Article 19 of that Decree:
  1. Business affairs regarding requesting a diagnosis and evaluation prior to filing a request for a medical treatment order under Article 4(2) and Article 22(2)5 of the Act;
  2. Business affairs regarding requesting an investigation prior to filing a request for a medical treatment order under Article 5(1) and Article 22(2)3 of the Act;
  3. Business affairs regarding issuing directions for the execution of a medical treatment order under Article 13 of the Act;
  4. Business affairs regarding issuing directions for execution pursuant to a decision on the extension of a treatment period, etc. under Articles 13 and 16 of the Act;
  5. Business affairs regarding verifying consent to pharmacologic treatment under Article 22(2)5 of the Act.
  (2) Where unavoidable for performing the following business affairs, the head of a correctional institution, juvenile correctional institution, detention center, or medical treatment and custody facility may process data containing personal information under paragraph (1):
  1. Business affairs regarding notifying a scheduled release under Article 11(2) and Article 22(12) of the Act;
  2. Business affairs regarding releasing a person from detention under Article 14(5)1 of the Act;
  3. Business affairs regarding verifying consent to pharmacologic treatment under Article 22(2)1 of the Act;
  4. Business affairs regarding notifying the fact of consent to pharmacologic treatment and related matters under Article 22(2)1 of the Act;
  5. Business affairs regarding transferring a person who has been issued a medical treatment order under Article 10(2) and Article 12(1)1 of this Decree.
  (3) Where unavoidable for performing business affairs regarding decisions on provisional rescission under Article 18(4) and (5) of the Act or the revocation of provisional rescission of a medical treatment order under Article 19(1) of the Act, the Review Commission may process data containing personal information under paragraph (1).
  (4) Where unavoidable for performing the following business affairs, the Medical Treatment and Custody Deliberation Committee may process data containing personal information under paragraph (1): <Amended on Dec. 29, 2017>
  1. Business affairs regarding decisions on exemption from execution of a medical treatment order under Article 8-3(1) of the Act;
  2. Business affairs regarding notifications of decisions on exemption from execution of a medical treatment order under Article 8-4 of the Act;
  3. Business affairs regarding decisions to impose a medical treatment order under Article 25(1) of the Act;
  4. Business affairs regarding requesting a diagnosis and evaluation under Article 25(2) of the Act;
  5. Business affairs regarding notifications of decisions to impose a medical treatment order under Article 25(3) of the Act.
  (5) Where unavoidable for performing the following business affairs, the head of a probation office or a probation officer may process data containing personal information under paragraph (1): <Amended on Dec. 29, 2017>
  1. Business affairs regarding investigations under Article 8-2(5) of the Act and Article 4-2(2) of this Decree;
  2. Business affairs regarding notifications for execution of a medical treatment order under Article 13 of the Act and Article 12(1) of this Decree;
  3. Business affairs regarding explanations concerning pharmacologic treatment under Article 14(2) of the Act;
  4. Business affairs regarding requesting examinations as to whether counteracting medication has been administered under Article 15(1) of the Act;
  5. Business affairs regarding the receipt of reports from a person who has been issued a medical treatment order under Article 15(2) of the Act and Article 14(2) of this Decree;
  6. Business affairs regarding reports and permission concerning change of residence, etc. under Article 15(3) of the Act;
  7. Business affairs regarding applications for provisional rescission of a medical treatment order under Article 17(1) of the Act or the revocation thereof under Article 19(1) of the Act;
  8. Business affairs regarding the bearing of medical treatment expenses under Article 24 of the Act;
  9. Business affairs regarding the submission of data necessary for verifying the financial ability to bear medical treatment expenses under Article 24 of the Act and Article 26(5) of this Decree;
  10. Business affairs regarding applications for approval of temporary suspension of medication administration under Article 11(3) of this Decree;
  11. Business affairs regarding reports on treatment for adverse effects, etc. under Article 11(5) of this Decree;
  12. Business affairs regarding requests for notification of immigration and emigration records under Article 14(3) of this Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 6, 2012]
